Fitted Distance-Removal Model with a Fixed-Range Abundance Field

Source: R/gdr_response_field_class.R, R/gdr_response_field_covariance.R, R/gdr_response_field_predict.R
unmarkedFitGDRField-class.Rd

The class of object returned by fit_gdr_response_field(). It extends the unmarkedFitGDR class of unmarked with one slot, response_field, which holds the field geometry, the covariance retained from the fit and its diagnostics. Most unmarked methods work as usual. The methods listed below are replaced or stopped because the inherited versions do not handle the correlated field.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'unmarkedFitGDRField'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, type, method = c("normal", "profile"))

# S4 method for class 'unmarkedFitGDRField'
update(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'unmarkedFitGDRField'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, ...)

# S4 method for class 'unmarkedFitGDRField'
profile(fitted, ...)

# S4 method for class 'unmarkedFitGDRField'
ranef(object, ...)

Arguments

object, fitted

A fitted unmarkedFitGDRField object.

parm, type, level, method

Arguments of confint(). type names the component ("lambda", "dist" or "rem"), parm optionally selects coefficients within it, and level is the confidence level (default 0.95). method = "normal" (the default) gives Wald intervals from the retained covariance. method = "profile" stops for this class.

...

Not used. The stopped methods ignore extra arguments.

nsim, seed

Not used. simulate() stops for this class.

Slots

response_field

A named list. The elements you are most likely to read are:

  • definition: the field definition, with covariance ("exponential"), the supplied range, range_estimated (always FALSE), the linear units of the CRS, state_count (the number of blocks) and survey_count.

  • coords: the survey coordinates supplied to fit_gdr_response_field(), one row per survey. block gives each survey's block number, and crs holds the CRS as WKT text.

  • point: the complete parameter vector at the optimum, named by TMB block. It holds the fixed coefficients (beta_*, link scale), the log SDs (lsigma_*) and the block deviations in their internal whitened form (b_lambda).

  • joint_covariance: the covariance matrix of point, the inverse of the joint precision returned by TMB::sdreport().

  • lower: the lower Cholesky factor of the block correlation matrix. Multiplying the whitened deviations by lower gives the physical field values reported by coef().

  • diagnostics: the checks of the selected start, such as pdHess, maximum_absolute_gradient, conditional_latent_maximum_absolute_gradient and conditional_latent_Newton_decrement.

  • settings: the evaluated tmb_settings. audit_file is the path of the final audit record, and max_memory_mb is the planning budget used by predict().

The remaining elements are frozen design recipes and SHA-256 fingerprints. Every method checks them before use and stops if any has changed, so do not edit this slot.

Methods for this class

MethodBehavior
coef(), logLik(), unmarked::sigma(), summary()Inherited from unmarked. Field values reported by coef(fixedOnly = FALSE) are physical deviations on the log density scale
predict()Replaced. See predict,unmarkedFitGDRField-method
vcov()Replaced. See vcov,unmarkedFitGDRField-method
confint()Normal (Wald) intervals from the retained covariance. method = "profile" stops
update()Stops. Refit through make_gdr_refitter(), which keeps the field
simulate(), profile(), ranef()Stop. They are not available for this class

See fit_gdr_response_field() for a table that locates each parameter and its scale, and vignette("v12-distance-removal", package = "multiScaleR") for a worked example.

See also

fit_gdr_response_field(), make_gdr_refitter(), response_field_geometry()

Examples

# \donttest{
# The field needs unmarked 1.5.2 and TMB 1.9.25.
if (requireNamespace("TMB", quietly = TRUE) &&
    utils::packageVersion("unmarked") == "1.5.2" &&
    utils::packageVersion("TMB") == "1.9.25") {
  # Eight survey blocks 1 km apart, six point counts in each
  block <- factor(rep(paste0("b", 1:8), each = 6))
  hab <- rep(seq(-1, 1, length.out = 6), 8)
  shift <- c(-0.4, -0.3, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.4)[block]
  sim <- sim_dat_gdr(density = exp(log(400) + 0.5 * hab + shift),
    distance_scale = 40, removal = 0.2, dist_breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75),
    interval_lengths = c(2, 3, 5), interval_units = "minutes",
    site_covs = data.frame(hab = hab, block = block), seed = 1)
  template <- unmarked::gdistremoval(lambdaformula = ~ hab + (1 | block),
    removalformula = ~ 1, distanceformula = ~ 1, data = sim$observed,
    keyfun = "halfnorm", mixture = "P", output = "density",
    unitsOut = "kmsq", K = 60, engine = "TMB",
    starts = c(log(400), 0, log(40), qlogis(0.2), log(0.3)))
  block_xy <- cbind(x = 500000 + 1000 * (as.integer(block) - 1),
                    y = 4400000)
  rownames(block_xy) <- rownames(unmarked::siteCovs(sim$observed))
  cold <- c("beta_lambda[1]" = log(300), "beta_lambda[2]" = 0,
            "beta_dist[1]" = log(30), "beta_rem[1]" = qlogis(0.4),
            "lsigma_lambda[1]" = log(0.5))
  settings <- list(method = "BFGS", se = TRUE, threads = 1L,
                   control = list(maxit = 2500L, reltol = 1e-10))
  field_fit <- fit_gdr_response_field(template, block_xy, crs = 32617,
    range = 2000, cold_starts = list(cold = cold),
    audit_dir = tempfile("gdr-field-"), tmb_settings = settings)

  # TRUE: the methods of unmarked still apply
  print(methods::is(field_fit, "unmarkedFitGDR"))
  # The supplied range, its units, and the number of blocks and surveys
  str(field_fit@response_field$definition[c("range", "units",
                                            "state_count", "survey_count")])
  # Wald limits for the abundance coefficients, on the log scale
  print(confint(field_fit, type = "lambda"))
}
#> [1] TRUE
#> List of 4
#>  $ range       : num 2000
#>  $ units       : chr "metre"
#>  $ state_count : int 8
#>  $ survey_count: int 48
#>                 0.025     0.975
#> lambda(Int) 5.6993885 6.5593710
#> lambda(hab) 0.2067472 0.6779487
# }
